item.title: Death at Ravenscroft Manor: A Murder Mystery Logic Grid
item.description:
You have nine clues and a dead lord. Clue one says Dr. Pryce wasn’t seen at 9:45. Fine. Clue three says he wasn’t seen at 9:30 either. Two ✕s later, the doctor’s row in the Time block has only two squares left, and clue eight is already whispering about which one. That narrowing is the reason people have been doing these on train rides for sixty years.

This one is a classic logic grid: every guest was in exactly one room, holding exactly one object, at exactly one time. Nothing is shared and nothing is left over. The clues never lie, and they’re enough to pin down every pairing without a single guess. The generator that built this puzzle rejected every clue set that needed trial and error.

item.title: The Blackwood Estate: A Victorian Murder Escape
item.description:
The front door booms shut behind you and a bolt slides home on the far side. You didn’t hear anyone follow you up the drive. Somewhere down the hall is a dead man, a locked desk and three people who all have a very good reason to be somewhere else. The coachman is clear about it: nobody leaves until someone is named.

This is a narrative escape game, a little like a choose-your-own-adventure book that fights back. You read, you choose where to go, and when you hit a lock you have to work out the combination from what you’ve seen. Everything you need is somewhere in the house.
